references.text: Jesus states the same principle in another context: 'But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first' ([ref:Matt 19:30|Matthew 19:30]). This is a direct parallel to Luke 13:30 and emphasizes God's overturning of human rankings.

At the conclusion of the parable of the workers in the vineyard, Jesus repeats the same statement: 'So the last will be first, and the first last' ([ref:Matt 20:16|Matthew 20:16]). The parable illustrates concretely how this principle works in God's kingdom.

We also find the same proverb in the Gospel of Mark: 'But many who are first will be last, and the last first' ([ref:Mark 10:31|Mark 10:31]). This confirms that this was a central theme in Jesus' teaching.

Jesus says that many will come from east and west and sit at the table with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven, while the children of the kingdom will be thrown out ([ref:Matt 8:11-12|Matthew 8:11-12]). This illustrates the same principle: Gentiles (the 'last') share in the kingdom, while many of Israel's children (the 'first') miss it.
'For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted' ([ref:Luk 14:11|Luke 14:11]). A related principle about God's overturning of human status and rank.

Paul explains how Gentile nations that did not pursue righteousness attained it through faith, while Israel, striving for the law of righteousness, did not reach it ([ref:Rom 9:30-31|Romans 9:30-31]). This is a theological elaboration of the principle that the last become first.

Jesus says to the chief priests and elders: 'Tax collectors and prostitutes enter God's kingdom before you' ([ref:Matt 21:31|Matthew 21:31]). Those considered last in religious rank go ahead of the religious leaders—a concrete illustration of Luke 13:30.

The immediately preceding context in [ref:Luk 13:28-29|Luke 13:28-29] shows that people from all corners of the earth will sit at the table in God's kingdom, while some who expected to be included are thrown out. Verse 30 summarizes this principle.
